name: Broken Object Level Authorization
description: APIs tend to expose endpoints that handle object identifiers, creating a wide attack surface of Object Level Access Control issues.

sub_tests.name: IDOR via sequential IDs
test_steps: Capture request with object ID
Increment/decrement ID
Check if other user's data returned

sub_tests.name: IDOR via UUID guessing
test_steps: Collect UUID patterns from responses
Check for UUID v1 predictability
Try leaked UUIDs from other endpoints

sub_tests.name: Horizontal privilege escalation via parameter tampering
test_steps: Authenticate as user A
Capture API request referencing user A's resource
Replace resource identifier with user B's resource
Verify unauthorized access

sub_tests.name: BOLA via GraphQL node queries
test_steps: Identify GraphQL node/nodes queries
Query objects by ID belonging to other users
Test relay-style global IDs for predictability

sub_tests.name: BOLA via file/document access
test_steps: Upload a file as user A and note returned URL/ID
Attempt to access/download file using user B's session
Test direct object references in download endpoints

name: Broken Authentication
description: Authentication mechanisms are often implemented incorrectly, allowing attackers to compromise authentication tokens or exploit implementation flaws to assume other user's identities.

sub_tests.name: Weak JWT validation
test_steps: Decode JWT and inspect header/payload
Test algorithm confusion (RS256 to HS256)
Test none algorithm bypass
Check if signature is validated

sub_tests.name: Credential stuffing and brute force
test_steps: Test login endpoint rate limiting
Attempt multiple failed logins
Check for account lockout mechanisms
Test with common credential lists

sub_tests.name: Token leakage in URL/logs
test_steps: Check if tokens are sent in URL query parameters
Inspect Referer headers for token leakage
Check server responses for token exposure in error messages

sub_tests.name: Missing authentication on endpoints
test_steps: Enumerate API endpoints
Send requests without authentication headers
Check for admin/internal endpoints accessible without auth

sub_tests.name: Password reset flow abuse
test_steps: Test password reset token predictability
Check if reset token can be reused
Test host header injection in reset emails
Verify rate limits on reset endpoint

name: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
description: Lack of or improper authorization validation at the object property level leads to information exposure or manipulation by unauthorized parties through mass assignment or excessive data exposure.

sub_tests.name: Mass assignment via extra properties
test_steps: Send POST/PUT request with additional properties not in the form
Include role/admin/privilege fields in request body
Check if server accepts and persists the extra fields

sub_tests.name: Excessive data exposure in responses
test_steps: Compare API response fields to what the UI displays
Check if sensitive fields are returned but hidden by frontend
Look for password hashes, tokens, or PII in responses

sub_tests.name: Property-level access control bypass
test_steps: Identify read-only properties in the API documentation
Attempt to modify read-only fields via PUT/PATCH
Test partial updates overwriting protected fields

sub_tests.name: GraphQL field-level exposure
test_steps: Run introspection query to discover all fields
Query sensitive fields on user/account types
Test if __typename reveals internal types

name: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
description: Satisfying API requests requires resources such as network bandwidth, CPU, memory, and storage. APIs are vulnerable when there are no limits on the size or number of resources that can be requested.

sub_tests.name: Missing rate limiting
test_steps: Send rapid sequential requests to the same endpoint
Check response headers for rate limit indicators
Test if rate limits are per-user, per-IP, or global
Test if rate limits can be bypassed with header manipulation

sub_tests.name: Resource-exhaustion via large payloads
test_steps: Send oversized JSON/XML body
Upload extremely large files
Test maximum query string length
Send deeply nested JSON structures

sub_tests.name: Pagination abuse
test_steps: Request extremely large page sizes
Test negative or zero page sizes
Check if total count queries are expensive
Test cursor-based vs offset-based pagination limits

sub_tests.name: GraphQL query complexity abuse
test_steps: Send deeply nested GraphQL queries
Test circular reference queries
Check for query depth limits
Test batch query execution
payloads: query { users { friends { friends { friends { name } } } } }

sub_tests.name: SMS/email bombing via API
test_steps: Trigger OTP/verification endpoint repeatedly
Test if SMS/email sending is rate limited per recipient
Check cost implications of mass sending

name: Broken Function Level Authorization
description: Complex access control policies with different hierarchies, groups, and roles, and an unclear separation between administrative and regular functions, tend to lead to authorization flaws.

sub_tests.name: Vertical privilege escalation
test_steps: Authenticate as regular user
Attempt to access admin-only API endpoints
Test changing HTTP method (GET to DELETE, PUT)
Test admin endpoints with regular user token

sub_tests.name: HTTP method tampering
test_steps: Change GET to PUT/DELETE/PATCH on resource endpoints
Test if different HTTP methods bypass authorization
Check if OPTIONS reveals allowed methods with weaker auth

sub_tests.name: API versioning authorization bypass
test_steps: Discover older API versions
Test if deprecated versions have weaker authorization
Check if v1 endpoints lack controls added to v2

sub_tests.name: Path traversal for function access
test_steps: Test path manipulation to reach admin functions
Try URL encoding variations
Test parameter pollution to bypass routing

name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
description: APIs vulnerable to this risk expose a business flow without compensating for the damage it can cause if used excessively in an automated manner. This doesn't necessarily come from implementation bugs.

sub_tests.name: Automated purchase/booking abuse
test_steps: Automate purchase flow via API
Test scalping/bulk buying without CAPTCHA
Check if business logic allows negative quantities/prices
Verify inventory management under concurrent requests

sub_tests.name: Comment/review spam
test_steps: Automate comment/review submission
Test if anti-bot mechanisms exist
Check for rate limiting on content creation
Test if CAPTCHA can be bypassed

sub_tests.name: Referral/coupon abuse
test_steps: Automate referral code generation and redemption
Test if same coupon can be applied multiple times
Check for race conditions in coupon redemption
Test self-referral loops

sub_tests.name: Account creation abuse
test_steps: Automate mass account creation
Test if email verification can be bypassed
Check for phone number reuse
Test disposable email acceptance

name: Server Side Request Forgery
description: SSRF flaws occur when an API fetches a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL. This allows an attacker to coerce the application to send requests to unexpected destinations.

sub_tests.name: SSRF to internal services
test_steps: Identify parameters accepting URLs
Test with internal IP addresses
Try cloud metadata endpoints
Test DNS rebinding attacks

sub_tests.name: SSRF via URL parsing inconsistencies
test_steps: Test URL parser bypass techniques
Try different URL schemes
Test open redirect chaining into SSRF
Use URL encoding tricks

sub_tests.name: SSRF via file upload/processing
test_steps: Upload SVG with external entity references
Upload document with remote resource links
Test PDF generation with external URLs
Upload HTML with iframe/script to internal resources

sub_tests.name: Blind SSRF detection
test_steps: Set up out-of-band callback server
Inject callback URL in all URL-accepting parameters
Monitor for DNS lookups and HTTP callbacks
Test timing-based SSRF detection

name: Security Misconfiguration
description: APIs and the systems supporting them typically contain complex configurations meant to make them more customizable. Misconfiguration can happen at any level of the API stack.

sub_tests.name: Verbose error messages
test_steps: Send malformed requests to trigger errors
Check for stack traces in responses
Test with invalid content types
Send requests to non-existent endpoints

sub_tests.name: CORS misconfiguration
test_steps: Test with Origin header set to attacker domain
Check Access-Control-Allow-Origin for wildcard
Test if credentials are allowed with wildcard origin
Check preflight response headers

sub_tests.name: Missing security headers
test_steps: Check for X-Content-Type-Options
Verify Strict-Transport-Security
Check Content-Security-Policy
Verify X-Frame-Options
Check Cache-Control for sensitive responses

sub_tests.name: Unnecessary HTTP methods enabled
test_steps: Send OPTIONS request to discover allowed methods
Test TRACE method for XST
Check if PUT/DELETE are enabled but unused
Test WebDAV methods

sub_tests.name: TLS/SSL misconfiguration
test_steps: Check for outdated TLS versions
Test for weak cipher suites
Verify certificate chain
Check for HTTP to HTTPS redirect

name: Improper Inventory Management
description: APIs tend to expose more endpoints than traditional web applications, making proper and updated documentation highly important. Hosts inventory and deployed API versions also play an important role.

sub_tests.name: Undocumented/shadow API endpoints
test_steps: Fuzz for hidden endpoints using wordlists
Check JavaScript files for API endpoint references
Test common admin/debug paths
Analyze mobile app traffic for undocumented APIs

sub_tests.name: Deprecated API version exposure
test_steps: Enumerate API versions (v1, v2, v3)
Test if old versions are still accessible
Compare security controls between versions
Check for deprecated endpoints with weaker security

sub_tests.name: Development/staging environment exposure
test_steps: Check for staging/dev subdomains
Test if development APIs are publicly accessible
Check for debug mode enabled on non-production
Verify environment-specific credentials

sub_tests.name: API documentation exposure
test_steps: Check for publicly accessible Swagger/OpenAPI docs
Test for GraphQL introspection enabled in production
Look for Postman collections or API blueprints
Check for auto-generated documentation endpoints

name: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
description: Developers tend to trust data received from third-party APIs more than user input. This is especially true for APIs offered by well-known companies. Because of that, developers tend to adopt weaker security standards.

sub_tests.name: Injection via third-party API responses
test_steps: Identify third-party API integrations
Test if responses from external APIs are sanitized
Inject payloads into data that flows through third-party APIs
Check for SQL injection via webhook data
payloads: Third-party profile name with XSS payload

sub_tests.name: SSRF via third-party redirects
test_steps: Identify API calls that follow redirects from third parties
Test if redirect targets are validated
Check for open redirect in third-party integrations
Test redirect chains leading to internal resources
payloads: OAuth callback redirect to internal host

sub_tests.name: Data integrity from untrusted sources
test_steps: Identify data flows from third-party APIs
Check if third-party data is validated/sanitized before storage
Test if third-party API responses are schema-validated
Check for type confusion from external data

sub_tests.name: Supply chain API compromise
test_steps: Inventory all third-party API dependencies
Check if API keys for third parties are properly scoped
Verify TLS validation on outbound API calls
Test if third-party API failures are handled securely
